Proposition. Binding isovector coefficient as the W_\lambda chiral residue (conditional)

Proposition (conditional on the identification BWVacuumRowIsHecke). Let the binding residual's isovector (bar-odd) part be the chiral residue of the W_\lambda Plancherel measure \mu(\lambda) = d_q(\lambda)^2/D^2 — i.e. the chiral part \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{chiral}} of the categorical mass (chirality-residue-mass-term) carried by the writhe's isovector content 2(Z-N) with chiral weight \kappa. Then the isovector mirror difference is

b(Z,N) - b(N,Z) \;=\; 4\,\kappa\,(Z-N),

independent of the mass number A = Z+N; equivalently the per-isospin coefficient b = 4\kappa is fixed by the single chiral weight \kappa.

The bar-odd writhe \sigma - \sigma^{-1} = 4Z = 2A + 2(Z-N) splits into an isoscalar part 2A and an isovector part 2(Z-N) with an A-independent slope (prop:mirror-baseline-cancellation). The chiral residue is the Reeb-involution-odd (\xi \mapsto -\xi) content (archimedean-chirality). The Bring surface supplies the chiral datum via the A_5 Galois twist \sqrt{5} \mapsto -\sqrt{5} (the five-fold chirality). Therefore, the chiral weight \kappa is the chiral part of the W_\lambda Plancherel measure. Its value corresponds to the open conjecture \mathtt{BWVacuumRowIsHecke} (\mathtt{bwS0}\,\lambda = d_q(\lambda)/D).

Consequence for the isovector closure. The binding-energy isovector closure is not an isolated problem. It derives from the same open conjecture as the W_\lambda identification. Once \kappa is derived there, the binding coefficient b = 4\kappa naturally follows. The empirical test then becomes the binding-side check that the isovector residual vanishes given that chiral residue — a rigid, no-fit criterion. The value \kappa emerges solely from the three calibrations and the identification \mathtt{BWVacuumRowIsHecke}. It is never tuned to data (the measured b \approx -1.75 represents the current error, not a target).
